ut_shinobe.blurb: Shinobe is a bolted cobble wall west of the town of Parowan, perched high on a canyon side and noticeably exposed. It holds a dozen sport routes with a solid middle-to-hard spread: a lone 5.8, a handful of 5.10s and 5.11s, and several 5.12s plus one 5.13 for the strong. The reddish conglomerate is packed with cobbles, so the movement resembles Maple Canyon, and belayers should stay alert to bits coming loose. The base has a good spot to stand, and the area is quiet, with very little traffic passing by.

ut_appendage_the.blurb: The Appendage is a very short wall in Rock Canyon above Provo, set slightly off the busiest stretch of canyon trail, so it can feel quieter than its neighbours. Twelve routes mix bolted lines with short cracks you can lead on gear, and most can also be top-roped. Grades run from easy to moderate for the bulk of the climbs, with a few harder sport lines up around 5.10 and 5.11. The landing area is roomy and there is plenty of seating, which suits newer climbers practising leading and placing gear.
ut_appendage_the.approach: Go past The Kitchen and the two cement retaining walls on the left side of the trail, cross the stream, then follow the left fork of the path up to the wall.

ut_dragon_arch.blurb: Dragon Arch is a buttress on the Alpenbock Loop in Little Cottonwood Canyon, outside Salt Lake City. It is mostly a trad crag, with a couple of sport lines mixed in. Of the twelve climbs, grades cluster from 5.8 through 5.11, with the majority in the 5.9 to 5.11 range and one very hard sport line near the top of the scale. The quartz monzonite is on the gritty side, so expect abrasive crack climbing, and the central right-facing crack system gives the buttress its best-known lines.

ut_small_one_the.blurb: The Small One is a bouldering sector in Right Fork, one of the canyons of Joe's Valley near Orangeville. It holds about a dozen problems on sandstone, mostly in the V1 to V4 range, with just a couple of harder ones, including a single problem up near V7. Right Fork as a whole is cold in the early morning, and sandstone here is weak when damp, so give it time to dry after any precipitation before pulling on holds.

_expect.name: Grotto & Base of Great White Throne

ut_grotto_base_of_great_white_throne.blurb: This trad cragging zone sits in the main canyon of Zion, at the foot of the Great White Throne. It has about a dozen routes on sandstone, ranging from 5.8 up to about 5.12, with most of the lines in the 5.9 to 5.11 band. Routes are one to three pitches, from hand-crack starters to longer corner and flake lines. The sandstone is fragile when wet, so wait out rain and damp ground.

ut_invert_offwidth_boulder_circuit.blurb: A string of inverted offwidth boulders strung out along Kane Creek Road near Moab, running from the Hurrah Pass turnoff toward the Moab Rim trail. The twelve problems are on sandstone and suit anyone who wants to practise upside-down offwidth technique. Most sit between V0 and V2, with a few tougher V4 and V5 problems, and some of those are serious. Body size changes the difficulty a lot. Wet sandstone is easily damaged, so skip the circuit after rain.
